key_insight: Storage capacity of a d×d linear associative memory is not determined solely by matrix degrees of freedom (d^2) but critically depends on the retrieval criterion: top-1 (winner-take-all) retrieval requires a logarithmic model-size factor, while alternative (listwise) retrieval rules yield qualitatively different, often lower, capacity thresholds.
problem_solved: Determines how many key–value associations a linear memory can reliably store and retrieve, and precisely characterizes how that capacity changes with different retrieval criteria (e.g., top-1 vs listwise) in an isotropic Gaussian model.
method: Model: analyze an isotropic Gaussian model of stored key–value pairs and a correlation-matrix (superposed outer-product) memory construction.
Theoretical analysis: derive sharp, asymptotic capacity thresholds for retrieval success under different retrieval criteria (proving d^2 ≍ n log n is necessary for top-1 retrieval).
Rigorous probabilistic and asymptotic techniques to characterize extreme-value/distractor behavior and the resulting phase transitions in retrieval performance.
impact: Provides precise design guidance for memory-augmented models and associative-memory architectures by quantifying trade-offs between model size, retrieval rule, and reliable storage capacity; helps practitioners choose retrieval strategies to meet memory or scaling constraints.
visual_elements: Scaling plot: axes d^2 (model size) vs n (number of items) showing sharp threshold lines (e.g., d^2 ≍ n log n) separating success/failure regions for top-1 vs listwise retrieval.
Schematic diagram: memory construction as superposition of outer products into a d×d matrix, with arrows showing query → retrieval.
Comparison panel: winner-take-all (single top match) vs listwise retrieval (return top-k) with illustrative distractors and success/failure cases.
Bar/line chart: retrieval accuracy vs stored items for different retrieval criteria, highlighting phase transition behavior.
paper_title: Sharp Capacity Thresholds in Linear Associative Memory: From Winner-Take-All to Listwise Retrieval
paper_authors: Nicholas Barnfield, Juno Kim, Eshaan Nichani, Jason D. Lee, Yue M. Lu
